name: The Backfire Awards
scope: The Backfire Awards site at backfireawards.com: the feed of nominee posts and Murphys, the carousels and their Instagram exports, The Midgley and The Murphy pages, the Categoric Table, search, the guidelines and terms, the Weekly Oops, and the merch.
colorNote: Warm 1970s retro futurism, matching the rocket merch: aubergine and ivory grounds, tangerine for the one call to action, rust for oops, dusty turquoise for links. Each category has an earth tone. Type stays Big Shoulders Display, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono. Every color has a night value. The site switches looks with html[data-look]; 70s is the approved look, classic is the earlier cool palette.

type.spec: Uppercase. Card and page headlines in 900, nominee names in 800; element tile symbols and the Bf mark in 900. Kept from the original kit; it pairs with the 1970s palette.

type.sample: A list of inventions and decisions that solved one problem and caused another.
type.spec: 15px, line-height 1.55. The charter quote at 19px. Buttons in 600.

type.sample: For outstanding achievement in unintended consequences
type.spec: Labels, the tagline, years, vote counts and the element tile. 11 to 13px, 500, uppercase, tracked .06 to .1em. Counts use tabular numerals.

exemplar.headline: For outstanding achievement in unintended consequences
exemplar.body: A list of inventions and decisions that solved one problem and caused another. You vote on them, argue about them in the comments, and add your own.

rules.detail: The joke is the award itself. The copy stays plain and factual and lets the facts carry the irony.
A nominee has to have worked. Say what problem it solved before saying what it caused.
State whether the harm was knowable, unforeseeable, partly knowable or still contested, and stick to documented effects.
Describe the decision and its effects. Leave out motives, character and private life, and nominate only public work.

rules.rule: Plain words for a general reader
rules.detail: Explain the chemistry or policy in a sentence a reader without the background can follow, as the Midgley page does.

rules.rule: Prose to argue, lists to scan
rules.detail: Argue a nomination in sentences. Criteria, moderation rules and fields go in lists.
Write year ranges as 1889 to 1944. Use commas, colons, periods or parentheses instead of em and en dashes.

gaps: There is no logo file for the full element mark: the masthead tile is drawn in HTML and CSS, and the only SVG is the favicon, which carries Mg alone.
The favicon sets Mg as live text in Arial Narrow, not Big Shoulders Display, and the text is not outlined, so it renders differently by platform.
The repository is named midgely-awards while the site, the package and the Pages project spell it Midgley.
The home page and Midgley page screenshots in images/ show the earlier classic look.
Avocado and muted rose are illustration colors; no text pairing has been measured for them.
